title: Contributions & Donor Restrictions
description: Account for contributions, donor-imposed restrictions, and releases from restriction.
html:
What Is a Contribution?

A contribution is generally a voluntary, nonreciprocal transfer of assets from a donor to a not-for-profit organization.

CONTRIBUTION = NONRECIPROCAL TRANSFER

Contribution vs. Exchange Transaction

The key question is whether the resource provider receives approximately equal value in return.

Contribution Donor Does Not Receive Commensurate Value
Exchange Transaction Each Party Receives Commensurate Value
Example

A supporter gives a charity $25,000 and receives nothing of comparable value.

This is generally a contribution.

Unconditional Contributions

An unconditional contribution is generally recognized when the contribution is made or promised, subject to the applicable recognition requirements.

After determining that a contribution is unconditional, determine whether the donor imposed a restriction.

STEP 1 IS IT A CONTRIBUTION? STEP 2 IS IT CONDITIONAL? STEP 3 DOES IT HAVE A DONOR RESTRICTION?

Contribution Without Donor Restrictions

Assume a donor gives an organization $60,000 and allows the organization to use the money for any appropriate purpose.

$60,000 CONTRIBUTION → WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Contribution With a Purpose Restriction

Assume a donor contributes $120,000 and requires that the funds be used for a literacy program.

DONOR SPECIFIES PURPOSE → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Contribution With a Time Restriction

A donor may also restrict when the organization can use contributed resources.

Example

On December 1, a donor makes an unconditional promise to give $50,000 that is payable in the following year.

The promise may carry a donor-imposed time restriction until the future period.

Restrictions Affect Classification

A donor restriction generally affects which net asset class receives the contribution.

A restriction does not necessarily mean contribution revenue should wait until the restriction is satisfied.

UNCONDITIONAL CONTRIBUTION + DONOR RESTRICTION → RECOGNIZE IN NET ASSETS WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Restriction vs. Condition

These concepts must not be confused.

Restriction Limits How or When Resources May Be Used
Condition Must Generally Be Overcome Before Contribution Revenue Is Recognized

Important

A donor restriction and a donor condition are not the same thing.

Release From Restriction

When the organization satisfies a donor's purpose restriction or a time restriction expires, the related amount is generally reclassified from net assets with donor restrictions to net assets without donor restrictions.

RESTRICTION SATISFIED WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS ↓ WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS ↑

Example — Release

A charity previously received $100,000 restricted by the donor for medical research.

During the current year, the charity incurs $100,000 of qualifying medical research expenses.

With Donor Restrictions − $100,000
Without Donor Restrictions + $100,000

This is a release from restriction. It is not a second contribution.

Donor Intent Matters

When analyzing a CPA question, carefully identify the donor's instructions.

  • "Use wherever needed" → generally without donor restrictions.
  • "Use for scholarships" → purpose restriction.
  • "Use next year" → time restriction.
  • "Maintain the principal" → donor restriction associated with an endowment.

Numerical Example

During the year, an NFP receives:

Unrestricted Contribution $70,000
Donor-Restricted Contribution $130,000
TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS $70,000 + $130,000 = $200,000

The organization recognizes $200,000 of contributions, but the amounts are reported in different net asset classes based on the donor restrictions.

CPA Memory Rule

RESTRICTION = RECOGNIZE, BUT CLASSIFY CONDITION = WAIT UNTIL THE BARRIER IS SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME

Key Takeaways

  • Contributions are generally nonreciprocal.
  • Unconditional contributions are generally recognized when made or promised.
  • Donor restrictions affect net asset classification.
  • Restrictions and conditions are different concepts.
  • Satisfying a restriction generally creates a release from restriction.

quiz.prompt: A donor unconditionally contributes $90,000 to an NFP and requires that the funds be used only for its youth education program. At the date of contribution, how should the NFP generally report the contribution?

choices.text: Do not recognize revenue until the money is spent
Recognize $90,000 in net assets without donor restrictions
Recognize $90,000 in net assets with donor restrictions

quiz.explanation: The contribution is unconditional, so it is generally recognized when made. Because the donor imposed a purpose restriction, it is reported within net assets with donor restrictions.

objectives: Explain contributions & donor restrictions and its underlying principles.
